SABER 1.2.0 binary used for every SABER 1.2 row: sha256 f2da505c17db56df991a4ca01a028c9e9fa1c655c76d447e007cf9f0cf98cfee
(rustc 1.75.0, cargo build --release; built from the saber-1.2.0 source as of the
benchmark run; the changes made afterwards are listed at the end of this file).

The session's container moved twice during the final run (2026-10-18), so the
results come from three 2-vCPU virtual machines. Every section was measured
completely on one of them, and every timing record carries `cpu` and `host`:
  host A1  until 21:15   Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 33 MiB L3   scop, decoy, mmseqs, index
  host B   21:18-21:44   Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 260 MiB L3  multi, threads, sweep
  host A2  from 21:47    Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 33 MiB L3   translated, lowc
                         (same CPU model as A1, different VM instance)
environment_hostA1.txt and environment_hostA2.txt were written by the env
section on A1 and A2; environment_hostB.txt was recorded by hand on B. Records written before runbench.py stored the CPU were
labelled from their timestamps. Baseline (SABER 1.0.2, 1.1.0) and DIAMOND
2.2.8 rows of the A1 sections were measured earlier on A1 with identical
commands and reused (REUSE=1); every SABER 1.2 row was re-measured with the
binary above. Compare timings only within a section.

Source changes after the benchmark run, made in response to an independent
review of the release (none touches seeding, scoring or statistics):
  * traceback fallback (src/search/engine.rs): when the band over a candidate
    region's diagonals would exceed the traceback memory cap, the traceback is
    redone from a band around the optimum's end cell (found by a score-only
    pass) instead of reporting the best partial alignment. Changes 9 of the
    4,712 long-protein alignments (all to higher scores; e.g. an 8,081-residue
    self-alignment that the benchmarked binary reported as a 583-bit repeat
    alignment) and no output of any other benchmark workload (none of them hit
    the cap); counter end_anchored_tracebacks
  * SAM NM = mismatches + inserted and deleted residues (src/io/output.rs)
  * --mismatch accepts negative values as a separate argument (src/bin/main.rs)
  * --outfmt bam prints a note that it writes SAM text (src/bin/main.rs)
  * --genetic-code archaeal = NCBI table 11; table 15 = blepharisma / 15
    (src/algorithm/translation.rs)
  * --doctor checks all 8 matrices (src/doctor.rs)
  * regression tests for the above; example scripts, Makefile, docs
The delivered source, built here with rustc 1.75.0 (cargo build --release),
gives sha256 b71102daf1891d4a70d2034beede564895ff12ea2c775135cecc808d5737fbbb
(the hash depends on the build path). Re-running 15 benchmark commands with it
reproduced the saved outputs of the benchmarked binary byte for byte for 14:
SCOP40 very-fast, fast, default, more-sensitive and legacy (36,311-106,215
lines each), MMseqs2 default, sensitive and --db, shuffled-decoy default,
blastx (115,378 lines), tblastn, two-domain queries and the low-complexity
set; the --db SCOP40 search equals the in-memory one. The 15th, long proteins,
differs in the 9 alignments above. results/recheck/ times the delivered build
against DIAMOND in one session (results/summary.md, "Re-check").
